pages.quiz:
HOME SCIENCE MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting.

8. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Consumer Protection.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Meals for Special Occasions? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Meals for Special Occasions.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Meals for Special Occasions.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Meals for Special Occasions.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Convenience Foods? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Convenience Foods.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Convenience Foods.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Convenience Foods.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Convenience Foods.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Careers in Food and Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Pastry Making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Yeast Products and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Careers in Food and Nutrition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Ice melting to water

2. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. A — Glucose and oxygen

5. D — 100 °C

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.

8. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.

10. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.

11. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Convenience Foods.

12. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pastry Making; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Yeast Products; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Careers in Food and Nutrition; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
